notes: delay_ticks is a .NET TimeSpan tick count (100 ns): 1 ms = 10000. The oracle builds TimeSpan.FromTicks(delay_ticks); the Rust port takes the same tick count.
now is the clock value returned by the injected timestamp function (set before the op runs). tick ops raise one frame with Timestamp = timestamp; an op's optional now is applied before the frame.
restart (case field, optional): the elapsed callback calls Start(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(delay_ms)) again, using the current now, while fired < until_fired (C# CallbackMayRestartTheTimer).

Output per op: running (IsRunning after the op), fired (cumulative elapsed count), fired_now (elapsed during this op), request_frame (start only: RequestFrame was called), threw (exception type name, only when thrown).

cases.name: Fires on the first frame at or after the deadline, exactly once
Start while running replaces the deadline
Stop cancels, releases the clock, and start requests a frame
Callback may restart the timer (three firings)
Negative delay fires on the next frame; disposed timer refuses to start
Zero delay fires on the first frame at the same instant
Half a millisecond rounds up to one tick
Frame before the deadline with a large tick rate
Timestamp far below the deadline never fires
Dispose while running stops and does not fire later
